title: The store facade is the only module that talks to the underlying engine; consumers use narrow verbs, not raw queries
description: One module (the store facade) imports the engine binding and holds the connection or file handle. Every other module in the process talks to persistence exclusively through named verbs exposed by the facade (insertX, findX, updateX, deleteX and their domain equivalents). No consumer imports the engine binding directly; no consumer constructs raw SQL or engine-native query objects and hands them to the facade for execution.
rationale: A single boundary between the domain and the engine is what makes swapping the engine possible, what makes testing the domain against an in-memory double possible, and what makes reasoning about which code paths touch persistence tractable. Raw-query passthrough defeats every one of those benefits without adding capability the facade cannot express.
